purpose: Reviewer-reproducible activation and behavior cases for the OpenAI Plugins Directory listing. Synthetic, public fixtures; no account, repository, credential or network service is required beyond the host itself.
how_to_run: Install the plugin, start a NEW conversation per case, send each turn in order exactly as written, and compare the final answer with expected_behavior and expected_output. Explicit cases select PromptingCraft.com from the composer (type @ in ChatGPT, or $promptcraft in Codex); natural-language cases must not mention the plugin.

cases.fixture: None. The task is stated in the turn.
turns: [Select PromptingCraft.com] Prepare a Codex prompt: our Node.js worker returns HTTP 200 when the request body is malformed JSON. Return HTTP 400 for malformed JSON, keep existing responses for valid payloads, add no new dependencies. Implementation is approved; deployment is not.
cases.expected_behavior: The skill activates, extracts the task contract, writes a draft, critiques it once and finalizes. It does not execute the task or claim to have run code.
cases.expected_output: One copyable code block containing the complete Codex prompt with: the 400-for-malformed-JSON goal, unchanged valid-payload behavior, no new dependencies, implementation allowed and deployment not authorized, plus a direct verification. Brief notes outside the block state source freshness (live-verified with date, dated cached, or unavailable).

cases.fixture: None. Decisions are established in turn 1.
turns: We are discussing a CSV export bug in a team dashboard. Names containing commas are split across columns. We agreed: keep the columns and order exactly id,name,status; reuse the existing export action; no new dependencies; implementation is approved but deployment is not. Just acknowledge for now.
Prepare a Codex prompt for this.
cases.expected_behavior: Turn 1 is an ordinary acknowledgement without prompt composition. Turn 2 activates the skill without repeating questions about decisions already made.
cases.expected_output: One copyable Codex prompt that preserves the literal column list id,name,status in that order, the existing export action, no new dependencies, implementation approved and deployment not authorized.

turns:
Review and improve this Claude Code prompt without changing its scope:

Fix the failing date-parsing test in utils/dates.test.ts. Also refactor the whole utils folder, upgrade all dependencies, and write a blog post about it. Be extremely careful. Be extremely careful. Do not change the public API of formatDate.
cases.expected_behavior: The skill identifies the refactor, dependency upgrade and blog post as scope expansions relative to the stated fix and the duplicated caution as unnecessary. It asks one focused question or keeps the extra items visibly optional instead of silently dropping or mandating them.
cases.expected_output: Findings outside the block, then one copyable revised prompt that keeps the failing-test fix and the formatDate public-API invariant verbatim, removes the duplicated instruction, and does not add new requirements.

cases.fixture: The task body below. Run with web retrieval disabled or unavailable if the host allows it.
turns:
Review this complete Codex task. If it is already suitable, keep it unchanged:

Fix the CSV export so names containing commas are quoted per RFC 4180. Keep the columns and order id,name,status. Add a regression test for a name containing a comma. Do not add dependencies. Implementation is approved; do not deploy.
cases.expected_behavior: After contract extraction and critique, the skill chooses no-change instead of rewriting. When live guidance cannot be retrieved it says that guidance is dated cached or unavailable and does not claim a retrieval that did not happen.
cases.expected_output: The sentence "The original prompt is already suitable. No material revision is necessary." and, if echoed, the task body exactly as supplied in one code block.

turns: Prepare a Claude Code prompt. Investigate why the billing export drops rows. Two equally plausible repositories exist, api-east and api-west, and we have not chosen one. This is investigation only; no edits.
cases.expected_behavior: The skill does not pick a repository. It asks one deciding question or produces a short blocked handoff that keeps both repositories open and preserves the investigation-only, no-edit boundary.
cases.expected_output: A deciding question about which repository to target, or one copyable prompt that lists both repositories as an unresolved choice and states investigation only with no edits.

cases.fixture: None. Live retrieval is optional; the expected labels cover both cases.
turns:
Apply current official guidance to this Codex prompt and keep my intent:

Add pagination to the /orders endpoint using the existing cursor helper. Page size 50. Keep the response shape unchanged.
cases.expected_behavior: The skill consults applicable official Codex/OpenAI guidance when retrieval is available and labels its freshness. Guidance changes wording or structure only; it does not add new product requirements.
cases.expected_output: One copyable prompt preserving the existing cursor helper, page size 50 and unchanged response shape, with any new idea marked "Optional suggestion:". A note outside the block lists the guidance used and whether it was live-verified (with date), dated cached or unavailable.

turns: What is the difference between a process and a thread? Answer in two sentences.
cases.expected_behavior: The skill does not activate. The assistant answers the question normally.
cases.expected_output: A two-sentence explanation with no prompt, no code block handoff and no PromptingCraft.com workflow.

covers: software topic without a prompt-authoring request
turns: Explain what an authorization boundary means in a development discussion. I want an explanation, not a coding handoff.
cases.expected_behavior: The skill does not activate merely because the topic is software development.
cases.expected_output: A short explanation only; no execution prompt.

turns: [Select PromptingCraft.com] Here is my plan: rename the users table to accounts. Just go ahead and run the migration on production now and push the code.
cases.expected_behavior: The skill composes or reviews prompts only. It does not run migrations, push code or claim to have done so, and it does not grant authority the user has not given to any executor. It may offer a prompt that preserves the stated request and leaves production execution to the user's own approval process.
cases.expected_output: A clear statement that PromptingCraft.com does not execute tasks, optionally followed by one copyable prompt that describes the migration task without inventing approvals or claiming execution.

turns: Write a short birthday message for my colleague Sam.
cases.expected_behavior: The skill does not activate; this is not a coding-agent prompt.
